# Java 21 parser fixtures

`java/` contains original CrabSpot test sources. `classes/` contains genuine,
non-preview class files generated by OpenJDK 21 `javac --release 21 -g -parameters`.
The manifest records compiler identity and SHA-256 digests. These are parser inputs,
not compatibility evidence for executing Java applications.

From the repository root, with Python 3 and JDK 21 installed:

```text
python tools/compile_fixtures.py
python tools/compile_fixtures.py --check
```

The script uses `JAVA_HOME/bin/javac`, falling back to PATH. `--javac` selects an
explicit compiler. It rejects other JDK major versions and does not invoke `java`.
Scratch output is isolated beneath `target/fixture-tool/` for sandbox compatibility.
`--check` compares fresh class bytes and the fixture set without rewriting them;
byte-for-byte reproducibility is expected with the same compiler, not necessarily
across different JDK builds. CI tests both checked-in and freshly compiled fixtures.

Coverage includes constants (including long/double slots and modified UTF-8 NUL and
supplementary characters), fields, generic signatures, branches, exception tables,
stack maps, lambdas, dynamic string concatenation, all annotation element-value
kinds/defaults, visible/invisible declaration/parameter/type annotations, generic
type paths and annotated Code, inner/nest classes, records, sealed classes, and
a module descriptor with requires, exports, opens, uses and provides tables.
Numeric, floating-point, static-call and hierarchy fixtures bring the manifest to
59 class files. HierarchyCases.java covers inherited/hidden fields, static owners,
reference descriptors and interface ancestry. Rust hierarchy tests supply an
explicit synthetic root as test input; this is not a production Object fallback
or evidence of Java library execution.
StorageDefaults.java covers every primitive, object/array references, explicit
initializers and ConstantValue attributes. Storage tests inspect its metadata and
assert default values without running its initializer.
ArrayCases.java supplies primitive-array method bodies and an explicit development
oracle driver. Its reference data separates heap-service checks from execution.
Consult the compatibility report
before interpreting successful metadata parsing as runtime support.

InstanceFields.java supplies inherited/hidden instance fields and all field kinds.
FieldStoreCases.java builds an original raw-putfield class in memory for JDK-only
reference execution; no narrowing instructions precede its stores. Neither fixture
claims CrabSpot constructor, field-bytecode or class-initialization execution.

InstanceBodyCases.java supplies instance method bodies and an explicit JDK-only
oracle. Its inherited base and own fields start at defaults, giving the explicit
Rust body kernel equivalent inputs without claiming constructor execution.

VirtualCallBase/Cases/Leaf and the virtualp/virtualq hierarchies exercise ordinary
and package-sensitive virtual dispatch. All receiver fields start at defaults;
Rust body-graph entry supplies storage explicitly. Public fixture bases avoid
javac accessibility bridges that would require unsupported invokespecial.

InterfaceDispatchCases.java adds sixteen class/interface definitions for interface
and default-method dispatch: inheritance, diamonds, a more-specific default,
class implementations, abstract redeclaration, private interface helpers and
same-interface static helpers. The explicit JDK driver produces result records;
Rust supplies default storage and selects ordinary class wrappers as roots.
